title: Selma Lagerlöf's birth chart
metaDescription: Selma Lagerlöf's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.9° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 19.1° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 27.9° Scorpio — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Moon. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 9.9° Sagittarius, Venus holds 29.4° Sagittarius, Mars holds 5.3° Aquarius — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a square within 0.8°. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable. Behind it, Mercury trine Saturn at 2.5°, and Jupiter square Neptune at 3.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Saturn while both square Pluto. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Taurus at 19.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Sagittarius at 9.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Gemini at 18.9° is in detriment; Saturn in Leo at 12.3° is in detriment. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 fire, 3 air, 2 water, 2 earth by element and 5 fixed, 5 mutable by mode. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.7° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 19.1°.
